+# snap_docker: a docker wrapper that, on the first `docker run`, copies the mounted HOME's
+# .codex/ to $T/snap (mode preserved) before handing over to the stub; the HOME itself is
+# deleted at exit.
+snap_docker() {
+  mv "$T/docker" "$T/docker.inner"
+  cat > "$T/docker" <<EOF
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+if [[ "\${1:-}" == run && ! -e "$T/snap" ]]; then
+  prev=""
+  for a in "\$@"; do
+    if [[ "\$prev" == -v && "\$a" == *:/home/evaluser* ]]; then mkdir -p "$T/snap"; cp -a "\${a%%:*}/.codex" "$T/snap/"; fi
+    prev="\$a"
+  done
+fi
+exec "$T/docker.inner" "\$@"
+EOF
+  chmod +x "$T/docker"
+}
+
+@test "container: KF-048 — the per-run auth.json carries the placeholder refresh token (never the host's), keeps every other key, mode 0600; the host file is untouched" {
+  cat > "$T/home/.codex/auth.json" <<'JSON'
+{"OPENAI_API_KEY": null, "auth_mode": "chatgpt", "last_refresh": "2026-10-18T00:00:00Z", "extra": {"k": 1},
+ "tokens": {"access_token": "x.y.z", "refresh_token": "R", "id_token": "i.d.t", "account_id": "acct-1"}}
+JSON
+  local before; before="$(python3 -I -c 'import hashlib,sys; print(hashlib.sha256(open(sys.argv[1],"rb").read()).hexdigest())' "$T/home/.codex/auth.json")"
+  snap_docker
+  run "$PR" --task-yaml "$BUILD" --arm a1_full --run-dir "$T/run" --run-id r1 --trial 1 --source-tree "$T/src" \
+    --suite-file "$T/suite.yaml" --executor container --docker-bin "$T/docker"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  local c="$T/snap/.codex/auth.json"
+  [ -f "$c" ]
+  [ "$(stat -c %a "$c")" = 600 ]
+  jq -e '.tokens.refresh_token == "loa-ablation-no-refresh-token"
+         and .tokens.access_token == "x.y.z" and .tokens.id_token == "i.d.t" and .tokens.account_id == "acct-1"
+         and has("OPENAI_API_KEY") and .auth_mode == "chatgpt" and .last_refresh == "2026-10-18T00:00:00Z"
+         and .extra.k == 1' "$c"
+  ! grep -q '"R"' "$c"
+  [ "$(cat "$T/snap/.codex/config.toml")" = "model = 'x'" ]
+  # the host file is byte-identical and still carries its refresh token
+  [ "$(python3 -I -c 'import hashlib,sys; print(hashlib.sha256(open(sys.argv[1],"rb").read()).hexdigest())' "$T/home/.codex/auth.json")" = "$before" ]
+  jq -e '.tokens.refresh_token == "R"' "$T/home/.codex/auth.json"
+  # no token value reaches the docker argv
+  ! tr '\0' '\n' < "$T/dlog/run-1.argv" | grep -qE 'x\.y\.z|i\.d\.t'
+}

+}

+}

+# --- KF-048: the codex access-token freshness pre-flight (Sprint 261) ------------------------
+# codex_auth <exp offset s> — a crafted auth.json whose access token is h.<base64url({"exp": now+offset})>.s;
+# prints the exp instant (ISO 8601 UTC)
+codex_auth() {
+  python3 -I - "$T/creds/.codex/auth.json" "$1" <<'PY'
+import base64, json, sys, time
+exp = int(time.time()) + int(sys.argv[2])
+pl = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(json.dumps({"exp": exp}).encode()).decode().rstrip("=")
+json.dump({"auth_mode": "chatgpt", "tokens": {"access_token": "h.%s.s" % pl, "refresh_token": "R", "account_id": "a"}},
+          open(sys.argv[1], "w"))
+print(time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime(exp)))
+PY
+}

+# --- KF-048: the codex access-token freshness pre-flight (Sprint 261) ------------------------
+# codex_auth <exp offset s> — a crafted auth.json whose access token is h.<base64url({"exp": now+offset})>.s;
+# prints the exp instant (ISO 8601 UTC)
+codex_auth() {
+  python3 -I - "$T/creds/.codex/auth.json" "$1" <<'PY'
+import base64, json, sys, time
+exp = int(time.time()) + int(sys.argv[2])
+pl = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(json.dumps({"exp": exp}).encode()).decode().rstrip("=")
+json.dump({"auth_mode": "chatgpt", "tokens": {"access_token": "h.%s.s" % pl, "refresh_token": "R", "account_id": "a"}},
+          open(sys.argv[1], "w"))
+print(time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime(exp)))
+PY
+}

head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1081 — remove_colliding builds the reserved basenames from every hidden overlay `.py` dest, and only `conftest.py` is discarded afterwards (line 1088). `__init__.py` is never dropped from the overlay set. So if a hidden overlay ships something like `tests/hidden/__init__.py`, every `__init__.py` the agent added anywhere (for example the one for a new source package) gets deleted before the tests run. The solution's imports then fail and a correct fix is graded as failing, which is the outcome 1.2.11 was meant to prevent. The fixture branch on line 1087 excludes `__init__.py`; the overlay branch needs the same exclusion.
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1092 — The removal is not limited to test modules or test directories. Any agent-added `.py` file anywhere in the tree whose basename matches a reserved name is unlinked, including source files. Reserved names include helpers such as `helpers.py` and `_oracle_x.py`, and any fixture file under `tests/`. An agent that adds `src/pkg/helpers.py` or `src/utils.py` loses part of its solution in every graded tree. Pytest's import-file-mismatch abort only involves collected test modules (`test_*.py` / `*_test.py`, plus same-named modules in package-less test dirs), so the scan should be limited to those.
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1080 — Overlay entries that are directories are only added to owned_dirs. The `.py` files inside them never reach `reserved`, so an agent test that shares a basename with a test in a directory-overlaid hidden suite is not removed and collection still aborts. The docstring promises that any hidden overlay `.py` basename is reserved; the directory case is silently uncovered.
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1019 — COLLIDING is incremented inside prepare(), and grade() calls prepare() once for each tree: final, base, implement and fix1. When gate snapshots are graded, the same agent file is counted once per tree, so grade.json colliding_tests_removed overstates the number of files removed. AG-35 only covers a run with no snapshots and does not catch this.
head/evals/harness/run-ablation.sh:817 — The KF-048 pre-flight refuses any auth.json that has no tokens.access_token. A codex host authenticated with an API key (OPENAI_API_KEY in auth.json, no ChatGPT tokens) has no expiring token at all, yet every non-smoke batch, resume and dry run that plans a codex-using arm now exits 2. When there is no tokens object, the check should be skipped (checked false) rather than refusing.
head/evals/harness/run-ablation.sh:806 — required_until sums watchdog_s over the whole plan, including arms that `uses_codex` just excluded (a0_bare) and, on --resume, trials that already have rows. The horizon is overstated, so a token that easily covers the codex-using work that remains can still be refused, for example on a late resume of a long batch. Only planned codex-arm trials that are still pending should count.
head/evals/harness/run-ablation.sh:502 — suite_kind_cap maps the value through `.[$k] // ""`, so an entry that is present but `false` (or null) becomes "" and quietly falls back to RUN_CAP. That contradicts the stated rule that a present but malformed per-kind entry is refused, never skipped. An entry of `0` also passes usd_ok, which yields `--max-run-usd 0`.
head/evals/tests/run-ablation.bats:95 — The comment says "A0 BARE stays 70 min … the PLAN + IMPLEMENT + 2 x FIX derivation (80) does not apply". The assertion two lines later expects 9600 s (80 min, `BARE = 15 + 35 + 2 x 15`), and RAB-27 asserts 80 min. The stale comment contradicts the behaviour the test pins down.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED
